title: Module quiz: Cost and capacity engineering

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Zephyr Games' team pins its requests to the most expensive model, which the gateway policy does not list as allowed. What does the gateway do?

options.text: Honours the pin, since the team chose that model deliberately
options.says: Ruled out because "The gateway uses the pin only when the policy allows that model".

options.text: Blocks the team for breaking the policy until it has been reviewed
options.says: Ruled out because the gateway does not punish: "Otherwise it uses the route for the task, and the default for a task the table does not know".

options.text: Uses the pin once and warns the platform team afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because there is no allowance for one exception, and the page says "because a pin is a request and not a right".

options.text: Routes by the table entry for the task, as that choice is a wish
options.says: A pin is honoured only when the policy allows it, and otherwise the table decides.

questions.stem: Scenario: Tallow Insurance's gateway sees a team at exactly 80 percent of its budget, and the next request is estimated to stay under 100 percent. What does admission return?

options.text: Allow, since the team has not yet passed its budget and nothing is wrong at this point
options.says: Ruled out because "Reaching 80 percent warns, and exactly 80 percent warns".

options.text: Warn, since the threshold is reached even though the spend remains inside the limit
options.says: Admission warns at 80 percent, and exactly 80 percent warns.

options.text: Block, because a team near its budget should not be given any more requests at all
options.says: Ruled out because a request that stays within budget does not block: "one that brings it exactly to the budget does not".

options.text: Warn only if the same team has also overspent in a previous month of the same year
options.says: Ruled out because admission takes "Given what a team has spent, its budget and the estimate for one more request", and not earlier months.

questions.stem: Scenario: Umber Retail's showback holds two usage lines for one team, each worth 0.4 of a cent. What amount in whole cents should be shown?

options.text: 0, because each line rounds down to nothing when it is taken on its own account
options.says: Ruled out because "rounding each row first gains or loses cents".

options.text: 2, because every line is rounded up so that none of the usage goes unbilled
options.says: Ruled out because rounding up each row gives 2 and is the loss of precision that "two rows of 0.4 cent are 1 cent together and 0 apart" shows.

options.text: 1, because rounding happens once after they are summed
options.says: The total is divided by a million and rounded once, so two rows of 0.4 cent are 1 cent.

options.text: 0.8, since fractions of a cent are kept for each team on the final screen
options.says: Ruled out because "The figure shown to a team is a whole number of cents".
